title: Acceptable sources for risk adjustment
question: Can this document support a diagnosis code for risk adjustment? Assign the code it supports, or 'no code' if it cannot be used.
note:
Chief Complaint
COPD follow-up.

HPI
Pt is a 71-year-old female presenting for a face-to-face office visit to evaluate chronic obstructive pulmonary disease. Pt reports stable breathing over the last month. Denies increased sputum production, increased dyspnea, or productive cough. Reports good compliance with current inhaler regimen. No new concerns at this time.

Medication List
1. Tiotropium inhaler daily
2. Lisinopril 10mg daily

Exam
Gen: Well-appearing, in no acute distress.
CV: RRR, CTAB.
Resp: Clear to auscultation bilaterally, no wheezes or rales.
Ext: No edema.
Vitals: BP 128/82, HR 74, RR 16, SpO2 96% on RA.

Assessment
1. COPD: Stable. Pt demonstrates good control with current medications.

Plan
1. Continue current inhaler as prescribed.
2. Follow-up in 4 months for routine clinic visit.

Electronically signed,
D. Kowalski, MD
05/12/2026
explanations: A signed face-to-face visit with an acceptable provider (MD, DO, NP or PA) that assesses COPD supports J44.9 (HCC 280).

distractors.why: The visit is face to face, signed with credentials and addresses COPD: it supports J44.9.
